display_name: DOJ/FTC Antitrust Guidelines for the Licensing of Intellectual Property (2017): the safety zone, the modes of analysis and the particular restraints, as what the agencies say they will do. Agency enforcement policy, not law.
seat: a party to an intellectual property licensing arrangement (the licensor or a licensee), asking what the agencies say they will do with it
scope: AGENCY ENFORCEMENT POLICY, NOT LAW: results say what the Department of Justice and the Federal Trade Commission say they will, may or would be likely to do, never what is lawful; each result name keeps its sentence's modal and voice (F25). Encoded: coverage (1.0, n.1, n.8); reach (2.1); market power never presumed from protection (2.2, 5.3); the concerns (3.1); whether a technology market (3.2.2, n.33; NOTHING when how the rights are licensed is not stated, F24) or research and development market (3.2.3) is analysed; the equal-share rules (3.2.2 via Example 2, 'will assign'; 3.2.3, 'may assign'); Example 3's four-entity screen; horizontal and vertical relationships (3.3, n.27); per se or rule of reason and the depth of the inquiry (3.4, 5.1, 5.5); exclusivity in effect and the two statements that a license 'generally' raises no concern (4.1.2); what the agencies do on their findings (4.2; NOTHING before a conclusion on the restraint's effect, F23); the 4.3 safety zone in full (facially anticompetitive, twenty percent of each relevant market significantly affected with exactly twenty inside, the goods-markets-only rule, the four-or-more criteria for technology and research and development markets without usable share data, n.58, n.86, which takes in n.85's transfers); price maintenance (5.2); tying (5.3); exclusive dealing (5.4); pool exclusion, future-technology terms and settlements (5.5); grantbacks (5.6); merger analysis of transfers (5.7's sale and exclusive license, n.85's 'may also apply', and Example 10's 'would apply' for an acquisition of a potential competitor); enforcement of invalid rights (6). Reported, never weighed: the considerations of 4.1.1, 4.2, 5.4 and 5.6. Inputs, never computed: market definition and shares, market power, close substitutes, efficiency-enhancing integration, reasonable necessity and every other finding the guidelines leave to the agencies. Answers NOTHING where the text states no outcome, for impossible shares in a market the safety zone considers once condition (1) is met (F27), for contradictory findings where the text does not say which wins, and for a trademark license.

forks.F1: 'collectively account for' is the sum of each party's own share
forks.F2: each relevant market considered must meet its criterion; the failing markets are named
forks.F4: 'facially anticompetitive' is decided by the type of restraint (or always or almost always harmful), whatever its integration
forks.F5: 3.4's list of per se types is open
forks.F6: with accurate share data, technology and research and development markets are tested at twenty percent
forks.F7: a goods market without usable share data has no criterion: NOTHING
forks.F8: three limbs for 5.7: the exclusive license read word for word ('will apply'), n.85's in-substance transfer ('may also apply'), and Example 10's acquisition of a potential competitor ('would apply'); n.86 takes n.85's transfers out of the safety zone too; the 5.7 field is 5.7's definition word for word, without 'in fact'
forks.F9: 'absent extraordinary circumstances' is kept in the result's name, not taken as an input
forks.F12: 5.6's offsetting effects are considered only once a significant reduction in incentives is determined
forks.F13: Example 3's screen and 4.3's research and development criterion use the same count
forks.F14: a trademark license: NOTHING (not covered, n.1)
forks.F15: when goods-market analysis is inadequate, goods markets are still considered (a goods market at 25 puts the restraint outside beside a passing technology market)
forks.F16: where the text says which of two exclusive inputs wins, it wins (blocked over substitute, 3.2.2 and Example 9; a clear less restrictive alternative over reasonable necessity, 4.2); otherwise NOTHING (3.4)
forks.F17: 4.1.2's 'only if' states nothing on its other side; exclusive dealing is a restraint on the licensee
forks.F18: Example 2's equal-share sentence is a general rule for technology markets
forks.F19: the safety zone's gates in the order coverage, n.58, merger analysis, condition (1), condition (2)
forks.F20: section 6: one input for both sentences' 'other elements'; fraud without them states nothing under the fraud sentence, and inequitable conduct is not a section 2 basis unless there are both fraud and the elements
forks.F21: 3.1 with no concern, and Example 3 with fewer than four and no significant risk: NOTHING (so Example 1's bottom line comes only through 4.1.2 and the supplied finding)
forks.F22: Example 3: a significant risk found wins even with four or more others
forks.F23: a three-valued conclusion on the restraint's effect (unlikely; has, or is likely to have; not yet concluded): 3.4 reads only the first; 4.2's later steps need the second, and it answers NOTHING before a conclusion (made 2026-11-25, NOTES.md section 13)
forks.F24: 3.2.2: a three-way input (marketed separately, 'may analyze'; an integral part of a marketed good, n.33's 'no need'; not stated, NOTHING); the equal share needs the first (made 2026-11-25, NOTES.md section 13)
forks.F25: result names keep the text's modal and voice: 3.3 'ordinarily will treat' for the horizontal component, 5.5 'In general', 5.5 'subject to challenge under the per se rule' only for the naked price-fixing and market division it names (any other per se type gets 3.4's words, attributed to 3.4), and the passives of 5.2 and 5.5's settlements (made 2026-11-25, NOTES.md section 13); 3.4's 'will' is kept against Examples 6 and 8
forks.F26: the bottom lines of Examples 1, 7 and 9 are supplied as the agencies' finding, not computed
forks.F27: an impossible share is passed over when condition (1) already fails or the market is not considered

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this against the guidelines. An independent test pass (tests-independent.l4, 152 assertions written from the text before the encoding was read) and an adversarial review were made on 2026-11-25; NOTES.md sections 11 to 13 say what each found, and that the renames held at first for the independent file were made the same day, with that file respelled in a commit of its own that changed no expected value. The fixtures for Examples 4, 5 and 9 are not independent of the 3.2.2 competitor test.
